I've been farming these 4 mu for 50 years, since I was 18. This plot is all my family has — me, my wife, and our son — so every decision is about making sure we have enough to eat and a little cash left over. I don't have money to waste, but I also can't afford a bad year. At my age, I know this land better than I know my own hands.

**Winter wheat**

I'll plant the wheat around October 12th. I've tried planting earlier, but wheat that gets too tall before winter freezes easier, and I lost a whole crop that way in the 1990s. I still remember it. I buy improved wheat seed from the county supply shop — I don't save my own seed because the yield drops. It costs about 25 yuan per mu, so roughly 100 yuan for my 4 mu.

For fertilizer, the extension agent always talks about soil testing, but I've watched these fields for half a century and I know what they need. At planting, I spread about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 bagged stuff. That's my base. Then in March, at jointing, I look at the wheat. If it's a bit yellow, I topdress with urea, about 40 jin per mu. That works out to roughly 12 kg of nitrogen per mu total. My neighbor Wang uses more, but his son sends money back from Shijiazhuang. I don't have that, so I stick to what I can afford.

I'll irrigate three times: once right after planting to help the seedlings settle, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling in May. Pumping from the well isn't free — electricity costs about 25 yuan each time for my plot — but three times is enough if spring rain is normal. Four times would be better, but that's another 25 yuan I don't have.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring when the weeds come up. If I see aphids later, I'll decide then whether to buy insecticide. No point spending money on something I might not need.

I expect about 400 kg per mu from the wheat. Last year I got 380, the year before 420. I'll be happy with 400.

**Summer maize**

The hard part is the turnaround. The combine harvests my wheat around June 8th-10th, and I have maybe five days to get the maize in the ground. At 68, I can't dig holes as fast as I used to. My wife helps, and our son takes time off from his factory job if he can. If the weather looks bad, I might hire one day of labor at 120 yuan to help with planting. I use hybrid maize seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has — at about 30 yuan per mu.

I don't have time for full tillage between wheat and maize. I do minimal tillage — maybe a quick pass with the rotary tiller if I can get it, or just plant into the wheat stubble. The soil is loose enough after harvest.

For maize fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 jin per mu, and then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage in July. Total nitrogen is about 10 kg per mu. Maize is more forgiving than wheat, and I need to save some cash for the wheat season next year.

I'll irrigate the maize twice if it's dry — once at planting if the soil is too dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. If summer rains are good, maybe only once. I watch the sky; I don't plan too far ahead.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide after planting and keep an eye out for corn borer. If I see damage, I'll buy insecticide, but I don't buy it ahead of time.

I expect about 450 kg per mu from the maize. Last year was 430.

**Labor and money**

My wife and I do most of the work ourselves. For wheat, we put in about 10 family days across the season, plus maybe 2 days hired help for the combine and any heavy work. For maize, about 8 family days, plus maybe 2 days hired help for planting or harvest if our son can't make it.

All in, my input costs this year will be around 1,400 yuan — seed, fertilizer, electricity for irrigation, pesticide, and a bit of hired labor. That's a lot of money for us. If I spent more on fertilizer, I might get more yield, but what if the weather turns bad? Then I'd have thrown away money I need for my wife's medicine. Better to be a little conservative and sleep at night.
